name: Opera cake
origin: Gateau Opera, created by the Parisian patisserie Dalloyau in the 1950s (or, by a competing account, Patisserie Clichy), named for its resemblance to a miniature stage; thin layers of almond joconde sponge with coffee syrup, coffee buttercream and chocolate ganache.

ingredients.note: ground almond is joconde's defining flour component, modelled with almond-kernel's own composition (packages/data/substances/almond-kernel.json) ground into flour form

process.name: whip almond-flour base
process.description: whip ground almond, icing sugar and whole eggs to a light foam

process.name: fold in flour and butter
process.description: fold in the wheat flour, then the small amount of melted butter

process.name: spread thin
process.description: spread thinly onto lined sheet trays for a fast, even bake

notes: The joconde sponge (Larousse Gastronomique's standard almond-sponge formula) is a genoise-family foam cake with roughly half its flour replaced by ground almond (almond-kernel, ground into flour form). Ratios are representative rather than one canonical published percentage table. The coffee syrup soak, coffee buttercream and chocolate ganache that define the assembled opera cake are separately-prepared components layered on after baking, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
